correctness.rationale: The private-pair lemma is an iff statement for all core graphs. Coalition partitions correspond exactly to incidence multigraphs with no singleton vertex cover and a size-two cover through each vertex. A pigeonhole argument rules out at least five vertices; a four-vertex loop and adjacency classification yields only 2K2, P4 and C4; each type attains four blocks. The surjection count and automorphism quotient are bijective and free, giving the closed formula. A directly executed verifier exhausts 120333 labeled vertex partitions at n=2..5 and compares true graph domination with private-pair coverage.

originality.rationale: The foundational ordinary coalition article and its tree sequel contain no leaf-corona partition classification. Connected-coalition papers establish a value of 2 for a strictly stronger connected predicate; they do not imply either the ordinary value 4 or the complete incidence-type partition count. Same-invariant, equivalent-object, broader-theorem, database, and prior-record searches found no dominating statement; an unindexed equivalent remains possible.
residual_risks: A non-indexed or differently named theorem about corona coalition partitions may already give a weaker or equivalent result.
The enumeration treats partitions of labeled vertices, and does not count orbits under automorphisms of the corona.
The n=1 boundary has a universal-vertex exception, so the theorem is only for n at least two.

value.rationale: This is a complete structural classification and exact counting theorem for the optimum coalition partitions of every leaf corona, insensitive to all possible changes in the base graph edges. The three incidence-graph types explain the universal value and supply a closed exponential enumerator. For connected bases it simultaneously exposes a uniform strict gap from the previously characterized connected-coalition value 2; the distinction is conceptually motivated, not an arbitrary parameter substitution.
